scope: Read-only collection; no repo/Git changes or architecture decision.
selectionWindow: c. 332–333 CE in dossier; off-map destination.
findings: Eusebius VC IV.8–13 reports an embassy from the Persian king and Constantine's concern for Christians in Persia; IV.9 introduces a letter addressed to Sapor and IV.9–13 preserves its text. Eusebius claims to translate the letter from Latin into Greek.

The passage does not date the letter or locate writing/dispatch in Nicomedia. It does not establish Persian-side receipt, response, or effects. Nicomedia as local map location is therefore not linked to the letter scene by the consulted source.

Kyle Smith (2016), chapter 1, treats the letter as probably authentic but notes debate and absence of independent attestation; estimates 324–337, earlier more likely. This gives no support for c.332–333 as a precise date.

Oxford ARCON institutional page identifies ancient Nicomedia with modern İzmit and describes a current archaeological mapping project, but not a published fourth-century city plan relevant to this event.
